memory_candidates.content: Lean 4 / Mathlib: `rw`/`simp only [singleLemma]` on a goal involving `ofLex (toLex literalPair)` over a `Prod.Lex` (e.g. `Q x_lex Z`) frequently fails to fire even though the target equation is `rfl`-provable by construction (`ofLex_toLex`/`toLex_ofLex` are proved `:= rfl` in Mathlib). The robust fix is to close via `exact`/`show` term-mode, which performs full-defeq (default transparency, iota-reducing) unification, rather than `rw`'s reducible-transparency syntactic matching. Pattern: replace `rw [ofLex_toLex]; <tactic>` with `exact <term proving the reduced statement>` or `show <defeq-normalized goal>` immediately before a concrete closing tactic (`norm_num`, `le_refl`, etc.). `norm_num` itself does NOT reliably whnf-unfold through such definitional layers on its own -- give it an explicitly-typed sub-term (`show X by norm_num` or `(by norm_num : X)`) rather than relying on its internal preprocessing to discover X from an obscured goal.

When a target theorem is provably equivalent (via existing in-tree completeness/soundness results) to an already-forbidden claim, formalize the equivalence as an unasserted Prop-to-Prop iff rather than attempting either side. This both documents the connection for future readers and closes off a second phrasing a future dispatch might attempt in good faith. Concretely: `TMCompleteX <-> ForwardX` proved via `completeness` (backward) and `soundness` + a validity-translation bridge (forward), with neither `TMCompleteX` nor `ForwardX` ever appearing as the conclusion of a `theorem`.

For a soundness theorem's `temporal_duality` case that needs swap-validity of every axiom, if the axiom set splits into a large 'ordinary' class (falls to a strictly weaker frame class already having full soundness+TD available) plus a small number of extension axioms with genuinely new semantic content, the ordinary class's swap-validity is FREE: build `DerivationTree.temporal_duality axiom_leaf` (applying the TD proof rule to the bare axiom at its own minimal frame class) and feed that into the weaker frame class's own soundness_valid theorem. This avoids re-deriving a whole parallel swap-semantics induction (a `SoundnessLemmas`-sized file) when the axiom set is small; only the genuinely-new extension axioms need a dedicated semantic swap lemma.
